items.text: Manage your own house and estate well.
items.quote: the business of the good economist at any rate to manage his own house or estate well.

items.text: Labor and expend care aright, sealing your ears to weak and soft seductions, so that your house is increased.
items.quote: He needs only to expend his care aright, sealing his ears to weak and soft seductions, and his house shall surely be increased.

items.text: See that the threshing is done evenly: turn the sheaves and push the untrodden corn under the animals' feet, keeping the floor smooth and finishing the work quickly.
items.quote: It is theirs to turn the sheaves, and ever and again to push the untrodden corn under the creatures' feet.

items.text: Keep all household goods in their appointed places, so that each thing is ready to hand and no time is lost.
items.quote: Stupid in all conscience would it be on our parts, my wife, if ... we ... fail to discover fair and fitting places, easy of access for our several goods!

items.text: Do not steal from your master or touch his goods; handle the produce faithfully.
items.quote: One thing is still required of him, and that is to hold aloof from property and goods which are his master's; he must not steal.

items.text: Train your household in justice and uprightness, using instruction, penalties, and rewards.
items.quote: I take a leaf now out of the laws of Draco and again another out of the laws of Solon... start my household on the path of uprightness.

items.text: Reward just and faithful servants with wealth and honor, treating them as free-born.
items.quote: I make them wealthy, and not with riches only, but in honour, as befits their gentle manliness.

items.text: Teach your wife the first principles of fair and noble conduct, and do not blame her for ignorance if you have not taught her.
items.quote: he has never tried to teach her the first principles of 'fair and noble' conduct... surely the husband will be justly held to blame.

items.text: Receive your husband's instruction, and do not delight in wrong-doing after you have been taught.
items.quote: supposing the wife to have received instruction from her husband and yet she delights in wrong-doing... the wife is justly held to blame.

items.text: Be a true helpmate and partner in the common estate, using economy and thrift so that the estate increases rather than being impoverished.
items.quote: a good wife, being as she is the partner in a common estate, must needs be her husband's counterpoise and counterpart for good.

items.text: Work the land diligently and provide for the household; do not let ignorance excuse idleness.
items.quote: He therefore that is unskilled in other money-making arts and will not dig, shows plainly he is minded to make his living by picking and stealing, or by begging alms.

items.text: Treat servants kindly, and let them share the good things you receive, so they become well disposed to you.
items.quote: By kindly treatment of him, to be sure, whenever the gods bestow abundance of good things upon us.

items.text: Train those you appoint as stewards in carefulness and diligent attention to your affairs.
items.quote: when I seek to appoint such men as bailiffs, I teach them also carefulness and application.

items.text: Honor a servant who is careful, and punish a servant who is negligent.
items.quote: When I see a man intent on carefulness, I praise and do my best to honour him.

items.text: Be careful yourself; supervise, test, and examine their work, for the master's eye makes servants diligent.
items.quote: he who would create a spirit of carefulness in others must have the skill himself to supervise the field of labour; to test, examine, scrutinise.

items.text: A steward must be loyal and well-disposed to his master and to all that belongs to him.
items.quote: the first thing he who is properly to take your place when absent must possess is goodwill towards you and yours.

items.text: Give careful and diligent attention to your master's business.
items.quote: I teach them also carefulness and application.

items.text: Do not cheat your wife in your shared estate with false money, sham necklaces, or dyed purples; show her your true fortune.
items.quote: without boasting of unreal possessions or concealing what we really have

items.text: Do not paint or anoint your body with pigments to seek your wife's embrace; present your natural, healthy body.
items.quote: would you have me first anoint myself with pigments, smear my eyes with patches of 'true flesh colour,' and so seek your embrace, like a cheating consort

items.text: Do not use white lead, rouge, or high-heeled shoes to deceive your husband; display your natural beauty in purity.
items.quote: thenceforward she never once indulged in any practice of the sort, but has striven to display the natural beauty of her person in its purity

items.text: Listen to your husband's words and carry out his wishes.
items.quote: the readiness with which she listened to my words and carried out my wishes

items.text: As true mistress, do not sit idle like a slave; stand at the loom, oversee the baking woman and housekeeper, inspect stores, knead dough, shake coverlets, and make beds.
items.quote: oversee the baking woman as she made the bread; to stand beside the housekeeper as she measured out her stores; to go tours of inspection

items.text: Inspect your servants' labor with an eye to every detail and improve their methods where you can.
items.quote: I inspect their various labours with an eye to every detail, and, whenever I can improve upon the present system, I introduce reform.

items.text: Tend the horse, lead him homeward, and carry from the country to town whatever the household needs.
items.quote: the boy gives the horse a roll, and leads him homewards, taking at the same time from the country to town whatever we may chance to need.

items.text: When a member of your household brings a charge or defense against another, listen, examine, and sift the truth.
items.quote: Some member of my household has some charge to bring... I have to listen and examine. I must try to sift the truth.

items.text: Arbitrate between close connections and press on them that it is their own interest to be friends, not foes.
items.quote: I must arbitrate between some close connections and endeavour to enforce the lesson that it is to their own interests to be friends not foes.

items.text: When your wife calls you to account, stand trial before her and accept her judgment.
items.quote: several times I have had to stand my trial and have judgment passed upon me... at my wife's bar.

items.text: Perform the outdoor works God has laid on you—plowing, sowing, planting, and herding—to supply the household.
items.quote: He laid upon his shoulders the outdoor works.

items.text: Guard the stores and do the indoor tasks, such as preparing food and making clothing.
items.quote: He imposed on woman the guardianship of the things imported from without.

items.text: Nurture the newborn babies, for God has entrusted their care to you.
items.quote: imposed upon her the nurture of new-born babies.

items.text: Defend the outdoor works and the household's goods from attack.
items.quote: he to whom the outdoor works belonged would need to defend them against malign attack.

items.text: Hold the house and estate in common, since the law makes spouses partners in children and property.
items.quote: the law establishes their common ownership of house and estate.

items.text: Each spouse must supply what the other lacks, making the pair more useful to itself.
items.quote: the married couple is made more useful to itself, the one fulfilling what the other lacks.

items.text: Support your father and mother in their old age.
items.quote: sons and daughters to support them in old age.

items.text: See that your laborers are devoted to the work on hand during the appointed time; do not neglect that duty.
items.quote: whether a man takes any pains at all to see that his labourers are devoted to the work on hand during the appointed time, or whether he neglects that duty.

items.text: Guard the house from ruin: give diligent heed to profitable work so that expenses do not outrun income.
items.quote: there is a steady outflow of expenses from the house, and, on the other, a lack of profitable works outside to meet expenses

items.text: Obey your father's direction: buy and improve untilled land, not an estate already under cultivation.
items.quote: my father would never suffer me to purchase an estate already under cultivation... nothing would satisfy him but I must purchase it.

items.text: Lend a willing ear to your husband's teaching and give all attention to his ordering of the household.
items.quote: lend a willing ear to what you tried thus earnestly to teach her

items.text: Show your wife the capacities of the house and the proper places of its contents, and arrange the home with her.
items.quote: I thought I ought to show her the capacities of our house.

items.text: Arrange the household goods in classes, assign each to its proper place, and set apart monthly and yearly stores.
items.quote: arranging the different articles of furniture in classes

items.text: Return safe and sound the tools entrusted to you when you have finished using them.
items.quote: return them safe and sound when done with

items.text: Give out stored goods as needed, remember to whom each was given, and restore each item to its place when it is returned.
items.quote: give out each thing as required; to recollect to whom she gave them; and when she got them back, to restore them severally to the places

items.text: Be self-restrained in food, wine, sleep, and dealings with men; be mindful, careful, and eager to protect your master's interests.
items.quote: on whose self-restraint we might depend, not only in the matters of food and wine and sleep, but also in her intercourse with men

items.text: Train your servants kindly: let them share your joys and sorrows, make them intelligent of the estate's affairs, give them a share in its success, and honor the just.
items.quote: by allowing her to share our joys... inviting her to sympathise in our sorrow... giving her a share in our successes

items.text: Separate the women's quarters from the men's by a bolted door, so that nothing is removed secretly and no servant bears a child without the household's knowledge and consent.
items.quote: nor children born and bred by our domestics without our knowledge and consent
items.conflict: Masters may not forbid servants lawful marriage or treat them as chattel (Heb 13:4; 1 Cor 7:9).

items.text: Teach your wife all that belongs to her appointed duties until she is capable of attending to them carefully.
items.quote: you taught your wife yourself ... until you had made her capable of attending carefully to her appointed duties

items.text: Listen to your husband's teaching and apply yourself to become all you ought to be.
items.quote: her whole manner showed that she would not be neglectful of what was taught her.

items.text: Join your spouse in sacrifice and prayer, vowing to become all you ought to be.
items.quote: did your wife join in sacrifice and prayer ... with many a vow registered to heaven to become all she ought to be
items.conflict: Pagan sacrifice and vows offered outside Christ conflict with the first commandment and Christ's sole mediation.

items.text: Seek the best partner of house and children for your daughter when you give her in marriage.
items.quote: with deliberate intent to discover ... the best partner of house and children we could find ... your parents ... made choice of me.

items.text: Take counsel together with your spouse how best to bring up your children.
items.quote: we will take counsel together how best to bring them up

items.text: Support and succor your parents in their old age.
items.quote: we find in them hereafter support and succour when ourselves are old

items.text: Treat all that you possess as a common fund, and strive to be the better partner rather than calculating who contributed more.
items.quote: our house here, which belongs like to both ... whichever of us proves the better partner ... contributes what is most worth having.

items.text: Manage your household affairs competently so that your husband may attend to affairs outside.
items.quote: my wife is quite capable of managing our domestic affairs without my aid

items.text: Train your children in self-control and modesty; this is the most important part of their upbringing.
items.quote: as regards control of appetite and self-indulgence, she had received the soundest education, and that I take to be the most important matter in the bringing-up of man or woman.

items.text: Mistress of the house, guard the order of your whole household: inspect the goods whenever you choose, and give praise and honor to the well-deserving and blame and correction to the offender.
items.quote: she must bestow, according to the power vested in her, praise and honour on the well-deserving, but blame and chastisement on him who stood in need thereof

items.text: Do not be annoyed when your husband lays on you more responsibility for the household goods than on the servants, because your share in preserving them is greater.
items.quote: she must not be annoyed should I seem to be enjoining upon her more trouble than upon any of our domestics

items.text: Fetch, carry, tend, and guard your master's goods, and use none of them except as he grants.
items.quote: they must fetch and carry, tend and guard them; nor have they the right to use a single one of them except the master grant it

items.text: Care for your own children rather than neglect them.
items.quote: any honest woman finds it easier to care for her own offspring than to neglect them

items.text: Create enthusiasm and ready obedience in your workpeople, rewarding the brave and correcting the disorderly.
items.quote: the husbandman, who means to win in his avocation, must see that he creates enthusiasm in his workpeople and a spirit of ready obedience

items.text: Exhort your laborers, and give them the hope and expectation that make even slaves stand willingly at their posts.
items.quote: the husbandman his labourers; nor because they are slaves do they less than free men need the lure of hope and happy expectation

items.text: Pay service to the gods with sacrifices on behalf of all your produce, livestock, and possessions.
items.quote: the wise and prudent will pay service to the gods on behalf of moist fruits and dry, on behalf of cattle and horses, sheep and goats
items.conflict: First Commandment: worship God alone; sacrifice to no other gods.

items.text: Before acting in war or husbandry, seek by sacrifices and omens to discover what you should and should not do.
items.quote: by dint of sacrifices and omens seek to discover what they should and what they should not do

items.text: Keep the household goods in order so that you can give him graciously whatever he asks for.
items.quote: if I ask you for anything, graciously to give it me

items.text: Do not blame your wife for being unable to find a thing if you handed the goods to her without assigning their places; take that fault as your own.
items.quote: you are not to blame for this, mine the fault was who handed over to your care the things without assigning them their places

items.text: Assign a definite place for each set of household goods with your spouse.
items.quote: let us, I say, select and assign the appropriate place for each set of things

items.text: Instruct the housekeeper to take each thing from its assigned place and to put it back there again.
items.quote: we will instruct the housekeeper that she is to take them out thence, and mind to put them back again there

items.text: Rule your servants so that they obey willingly and eagerly, not by compulsion or despotism.
items.quote: despotism over unwilling slaves, the heavenly ones give, as it seems to me, to those whom they deem worthy to live the life of Tantalus in Hades

items.text: Let your presence among the laborers stir fresh spirit, mutual rivalry, and keen ambition.
items.quote: if the sight of him is followed by a stir of movement, if there come upon each labourer fresh spirit, with mutual rivalry and keen ambition

items.text: Obey your master's commands eagerly, count obedience noble, and take pride in common toil.
items.quote: "It is nobler to obey" will be their maxim. They will exult in personal obedience and in common toil, where toil is needed, cheerily performed.

items.text: Show unflagging energy and eager intensity in the work done under authority.
items.quote: provided he is able to produce unflinching energy, intense and eager, for the work

items.text: Remain indoors, for a woman to remain indoors is nobler than to gad about abroad.
items.quote: for the woman to remain indoors is nobler than to gad about abroad

items.text: Send out those of your servants whose work is outside, and preside over those whose tasks are indoors.
items.quote: despatching to their toils without those of your domestics whose work lies there. Over those whose appointed tasks are wrought indoors, it will be your duty to preside

items.text: Receive what is brought in, apportion part for daily use, and store the rest so the year's supply is not spent in a month.
items.quote: yours to receive the stuffs brought in; yours to apportion part for daily use, and yours to make provision for the rest

items.text: See that clothing is made for those who need it, and make the dried corn fit and serviceable for food.
items.quote: to see that clothing is made for those who need; your duty also to see that the dried corn is rendered fit and serviceable for food

items.text: Tend any of the household who fall sick and nurse them back to health.
items.quote: Should any one of our household fall sick, it will be your care to see and tend them to the recovery of their health.

items.text: Provide for the household by seeing that goods are brought in from outside.
items.quote: without your provident care to see that the importations from without were duly made

items.text: Train any servant girl who knows nothing of carding wool or housekeeping, and make her skillful, loyal, and useful.
items.quote: to take some maiden who knows naught of carding wool and to make her proficient in the art

items.text: Reward the well-behaved servant with kindness, and correct the bad character when one appears.
items.quote: requite by kindness the well-behaved whose presence is a blessing to your house; or maybe to chasten the bad character

items.text: Be a better helpmate to your husband and a better guardian of the home.
items.quote: in proportion as you come to be a better helpmate to myself and to the children, a better guardian of our home

items.text: Learn the whole routine of the work and how to rule your fellow-workmen, so that you may be an efficient bailiff for your master.
items.quote: he must learn particulars--to know, that is, what things he has to do, and when and how to do them ... He must learn ... to rule his fellow-workmen.

items.text: Train your bailiff to know what he must do, when and how to do it, and to govern the other workmen.
items.quote: I try to educate them to that extent ... make them capable of rule

items.text: Govern free workers by reasoned persuasion, showing them that obedience serves their own interest.
items.quote: in man you have a creature still more open to persuasion through appeals to reason; only make it plain to him 'it is his interest to obey.'

items.text: Provide your workfolk with clothing and other necessary goods, giving the better things to the better worker as a mark of honor.
items.quote: the worse man will receive the worse things as a gift, the better man the better as a mark of honour.

items.text: Praise your bailiff when he apportions the best things to the most deserving.
items.quote: I praise my bailiffs when I know they have apportioned the best things among the most deserving.

items.text: Rebuke your bailiff when he grants favor through flattery or other unworthy means.
items.quote: if I see that some one is receiving preference by dint of flatteries or like unworthy means, I do not let the matter pass; I reprimand my bailiff roundly

items.text: Train slaves by gratifying their bodily appetites, as you would break a young animal to obey, rather than by reasoning with them.
items.quote: if they happen to be slaves, the more ignoble training of wild animals tamed to the lure will serve to teach obedience. Only gratify their bellies
items.conflict: Treat bondservants justly and fairly, not as mere animals (Eph. 6:9; Col. 4:1).
